subject: Architecture
title: Wind Tunnels Between Towers
description: Learn Wind Tunnels Between Towers in one minute.

hook.text: Some buildings create winds so strong that pedestrians get knocked off their feet.

buildup.text: Tall buildings funnel wind downward. Gaps between towers compress air into jet-like gusts.

discovery.text: The Bridgewater Place in Leeds created 80 mph gusts that flipped a truck and killed a pedestrian.

twist.text: Wind tunnel testing existed before these buildings. Some developers simply skipped the test.

climax.text: Cities now require wind studies for tall projects. Canopies and screens can tame the worst gusts.

punchline.text: The building looked great on paper. Nobody checked the wind.

quiz.question: What caused deadly wind gusts at Bridgewater Place?
options: The building's height funneled wind to street level
A gap in the facade created a whistling effect

details.summary: When clusters of towers are built without considering cumulative wind effects, the combined downwash and channeling can make entire neighborhoods uncomfortable or unsafe. Planning authorities now require pedestrian wind comfort assessments for tall building proposals in most developed cities.
details.whyItMatters: Individual wind assessments miss how towers interact. One building's wake hits another building, creating amplified effects that only appear when the full cluster exists — a problem that grows as cities build more towers on tight footprints.
takeaways: Tower clusters create cumulative wind effects worse than single buildings
Planning authorities now require wind comfort studies for tall proposals
Cumulative effects only reveal themselves once entire clusters are built

faq.question: How do tower clusters worsen wind problems?
faq.answer: Each tower deflects wind, creating a wake that hits neighboring buildings. Multiple towers create overlapping deflection patterns that channel and accelerate wind in unpredictable ways. The cumulative effect can be far worse than any individual building's impact, turning plazas into wind tunnels.

faq.question: How are wind problems assessed before construction?
faq.answer: Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations model airflow around proposed buildings, and physical wind tunnel testing uses scale models in controlled environments. Most major cities now require these studies as part of planning applications for buildings above a certain height.
